content:
Members received the report of the Director of Resources which
summarised the findings of the Council’s External
Auditor’s, Grant Thornton (GT), Audit Findings Report for
2024/25 (AFR), concerning the work undertaken on the Statement of
Accounts for 2024/25. The Committee had considered the Annual Audit
Report at its meeting in December, which explored the authority's
arrangements for achieving value for money.
 
Ade
Oyerinde, GT, proceeded to lead Members
through the AFR, attached to the report at Appendix A. The
Auditor’s opinion on the financial statements stated that it
was anticipated an unmodified (unqualified) opinion would be issued
in respect of the 2024/25 accounts. There were a small number of
areas yet to be finalised, but it was not anticipated these would
affect the resulting opinion.  Further
details on this work were outlined in the AFR.
 
The
Auditors had made six new recommendations to management following
their work, which were summarised on pages 38-40 of the
AFR.  Only one of these recommendations
was assessed as “high”, the remainder were
“medium” in status. 
Management had accepted all of the recommendations made.
 
The
AFR also included a follow up on previous recommendations made; all
had now been completed, with the exception of one which had been
partially completed (from 2023/24) and one remaining from
2022/23. 
 
           
A number of audit adjustments had been proposed which had been
considered and incorporated into the final version of the Financial
Statements (where appropriate), for consideration by the Committee.
No objections to the accounts had been made as a result of the
statutory Public Inspection.
 
The
Letter of Representation was also appended to the report which was
required to be submitted to the External Auditor, to formally and
publicly confirm the accuracy and completeness of the presented
Statement of Accounts. GT had made a minor amendment to the
document since publication, with the final table ‘Impact of
unadjusted misstatements in the prior year’ now not required.
Members were asked to approve management’s letter of
representation to be signed by the Section 151 Officer and the
Chair of the Audit Committee.
 
Members were given the opportunity to ask questions and the
following points were noted during the discussions:
 

·     
the uplift in fees;

·     
whilst the Council’s accounts were in a good
state, the Council was still facing financial problems going
forward which the savings programme would look to address;
and

·     
the high-risk recommendation detailed within the
action plan concerned systems administrators being able to also
post journals, presenting an issue of segregation of duties and
therefore a control weakness. The Council’s finance team was
a small team with posts currently vacant, but further recruitment
was due to take place, and the Council would explore the
feasibility of changing its administration approach. However, the
Director of Resources was satisfied with all journal entries, all
of which were reviewed by GT.
 
Members noted the AFR and approved the Letter of Representation,
as amended, to be signed by the Chair of the Audit Committee and
the Director of Resources (Section 151 Officer) on the approved
2024/25 Statement of Accounts.
 
RESOLVED: That:
 

1)    
the Audit Findings Report presented by Grant
Thornton be received and noted; and
 

2)    
the Letter of Representation, at Appendix B to the
report as amended, to be signed by the Chair of the Audit Committee
and the Director of Resources (Section 151 Officer) on the approved
2024/25 Statement of Accounts, be approved.
 
(Councillor Thomas declared an Other Registerable Interest in
this matter in so far as he was Chair of the Rother DC Housing
Company Ltd and in accordance with the Member’s Code of
Conduct, remained in the room during the consideration
thereof.)
topline: The Audit Committee has decided to approve the recommendations made by Grant Thornton in their Audit Findings Report for the Council's Statement of Accounts for 2024/25.

purpose:
The Committee previously considered the draft
Statement of Accounts in July. Grant Thornton have been undertaking
the statutory audit of the accounts. The audit work has now been
substantially finalised and the final amendments made to the
Statement of Accounts are outlined in this report, alongside
commentary on the core financial statements. The Audit Findings
Report for 2024/25 is also being considered at this
meeting.
content:
Members received the report of the Director of Resources on the
draft Statement of Accounts 2024/25, which outlined the final
amendments made following the External Audit, alongside commentary
on the core financial statements. The Committee previously
considered the draft Statement of Accounts for 2024/25 ahead of the
audit commencing. 
 
Grant Thornton (GT) had now substantially completed their work
on the 2024/25 accounts and anticipated issuing an unmodified
(unqualified) opinion on them. During their audit, GT identified a
few errors, as stated in the Audit Findings Report considered
elsewhere on the agenda; where relevant, these had been corrected
within the accounts presented in Appendix A to the report, and
summarised in paragraph 4 of the report. The Council did not adjust
two types of errors, the aggregate value of each being below
materiality level.
 
The
Code of Practice had required no major changes in the presentation
of the accounts for this financial year. 
 
The
report gave a brief description of the core financial statements
and the issues relating to them for Members’
information.
 
The
Balance Sheet showed that, overall, the financial position of the
Authority remained sound, with short term needs still being met.
However, the financial pressures and the level of Useable Reserves
able to support the budget continued to go down. This was being
addressed in the Medium-Term Financial Plan and the Council’s
programme of budget challenges, which was regularly monitored and
reported on to Members. 
 
Members had the opportunity to ask questions, and the following
points were noted during discussions:
 

·          
there were inconsistencies in the use of past and
present tense throughout the Statement of Accounts document, and
Members requested that this be reviewed;

·          
Members requested the word ‘relative’ be
replaced with ‘in comparison to’ when comparing the
Council to other local authorities;

·          
Members noted that the Council’s investment in
the Hermes Property Fund had now been returned, due to its merger
with another property fund and the Council not being eligible to
move its holding into the merged entity. The Council had incurred a
loss on its original investment;

·          
Members noted the high cost of bringing the
Blackfriars site forward for sale to the RDC Housing Company, which
had not been entirely grant funded. Careful consideration would
need to be taken concerning budgets for bringing forward further
available sites in the future; and

·          
undervaluation of properties did not change the
Council’s position, as values could go up or down, but could
have an impact on the following year’s resources and level of
reserves, as values would be reversed in the movement of reserves
so as not to have an effect on the
council tax payer.
 
Members were happy to approve the Council’s 2024/25
Statement of Accounts and agreed that delegated authority be
granted to the Section 151 Officer and Chair of Audit Committee to
approve any additional final amendments required.
 
Members congratulated officers for a helpful, easy to read and
valuable statement.
 
RESOLVED: That:
 

1)    
the Council’s 2024/25 Statement of Accounts be
approved; and
 

2)    
delegated authority be granted to the Section 151
Officer and Chair of Audit Committee to approve any additional
final amendments required.
 
(Councillor Barnes declared an Other Registrable Interest in
this matter as Vice Chair of Etchingham Parish Council, and in
accordance with the Members’ Code of Conduct remained in the
meeting for the consideration thereof.)
 
(Councillor Byrne declared an Other Registrable Interest in this
matter as a Member of Bexhill-on-Sea Town Council, and in
accordance with the Members’ Code of Conduct remained in the
meeting for the consideration thereof.)
 
(Councillor Thomas declared an Other Registrable Interest in
this matter as Chair of Rother DC Housing Company Ltd, and in
accordance with the Members’ Code of Conduct remained in the
meeting for the consideration thereof.)

Outline
planning permissions are granted subject to approval by the Council
of reserved matters before any development is commenced, which are
layout, scale, appearance, access and landscaping.  Unless otherwise stated, every planning permission
or outline planning permission is granted subject to the
development beginning within three years from the date of the
permission.  In regard to outline
permissions, reserved matters application for approval must be made
within three years from the date of the grant of outline
permission; and the development to which the permission relates
must begin no later than whichever is the later of the following
dates: the expiration of three years from the date of the grant of
outline permission or, the expiration of two years from the final
approval of the reserved matters, or in the case of approval on
different dates, the final approval of the last such matters to be
approved.
 
In certain circumstances the Planning Committee
will indicate that it is only prepared to grant or refuse planning
permission if, or unless, certain amendments to a proposal are
undertaken or subject to completion of outstanding
consultations.  In these circumstances
the Head of Planning can be given delegated authority to issue the
decision of the Planning Committee once the requirements of the
Committee have been satisfactorily complied with.  A delegated decision does not mean that planning
permission or refusal will automatically be issued.  If there are consultation objections,
difficulties, or negotiations are not satisfactorily concluded,
then the application will have to be reported back to the Planning
Committee.  This delegation also allows
the Head of Planning to negotiate and amend applications,
conditions, reasons for refusal and notes commensurate with the
instructions of the Committee.  Any
applications which are considered prior to the expiry of the
consultation reply period are automatically delegated for a
decision.
 
RESOLVED: That
the Planning Applications be determined as detailed
below.

content:
The
application was presented to the Planning Committee as it was a
major application and therefore in the public interest.
 
The
Planning Committee had visited the site and heard representations
from an objector and the Applicant. 
Comments from statutory and non?statutory consultees, as detailed
in the report, and an update sheet disseminated prior to the
meeting were also considered.
 
The
0.9ha application site formed part of the Jempsons Trading Estate, a long?established
commercial area comprising industrial and warehouse units on the
edge of Rye.  The site was allocated for
mixed?use redevelopment, including both housing and employment
space.  This proposal was one of three
applications forming a comprehensive scheme for 43 retirement
units, 16 dwellings and a food store.
 
The
application sought permission for a single?storey food store with a
retail area, warehouse, loading bay and staff facilities,
positioned in the south?west corner of the site, with customer
parking to the front. Improvements to the existing access junction
were included.  The proposed food store
development was considered inconsistent with the Development Plan,
contrary to Policy H6 of the Rye Neighbourhood Plan, and in
conflict with Policy EC7 of the Rother Local Plan Core
Strategy.   It was concluded that
the proposal would adversely affect the vitality and viability of
Rye town centre and undermine existing investment in the
area.  However, it accorded with Policy
RY1(iv) of the Rother Local Plan Core Strategy, which aimed to
broaden convenience retail provision in Rye by enabling
approximately 1,650sqm of additional net convenience floorspace
within or adjacent to the town centre. 
The development would generate local employment opportunities
supporting the local economy, and the Applicant was committed to
delivering a Local Employment and Skills Plan.  The additional benefits included provision for an
alternative food store, on-site biodiversity net gain, and
financial contributions towards pedestrian routes, bus stops, and
bus services.  Overall, the Planning
Officer’s opinion was that the benefits clearly outweighed
the identified conflicts with the Development Plan.
 
After deliberation, the Planning Committee supported the
Planning Officer’s recommendation for a food store in
Rye.  They agreed that although the site
was on the edge of town, it was still accessible to the town
centre.  Members felt the proposed
junction improvements would aid traffic calming and welcomed the
inclusion of two hours’ free parking, and provision for cycle
parking.  They noted the environmental
benefits, as residents currently travelled to other towns for
low?cost food stores, and agreed the development would support the
local economy, provide jobs, and improve the appearance of the
existing industrial area through new landscaping.  Proposed public transport links and services were
also recognised.  One concern about
potential flooding from the nearby river was raised, but officers
confirmed that suitable flood risk mitigation conditions had been
included.
 
Councillor Creaser moved the motion to GRANT
(Planning Permission) delegated subject to conditions and
the prior completion of a Section 106 Legal Agreement, as detailed
within the report.  This was seconded by
Councillor Stanger.  The motion was
declared CARRIED (8 for / unanimous).

(SECTION 106 AGREEMENT) TO SECURE THE FOLLOWING:

CONDITIONS:
 

1.

accordance with section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act

out in accordance with the following approved documents and

PRE-COMMENCEMENT CONDITIONS:
 

3.       
No development hereby permitted shall take place
(including demolition, ground works and vegetation clearance) until
the Applicant has secured the implementation of a programme of
archaeological works in accordance with a written scheme of
investigation which has been submitted to and approved in writing
by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To
ensure that the archaeological and historical interest of the site
is safeguarded and recorded, in accordance with Policy EN2 (vi) of
the Rother Local Plan Core Strategy.

 

4.       
No development hereby permitted shall take place
(including demolition, ground works and site clearance) until a
Construction Management Plan (CMP) has been submitted to and
approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Thereafter the
approved CMP shall be implemented and adhered to in full throughout
the entire construction period. The CMP shall provide details as
appropriate but not be restricted to the following matters:


a)   
Details (text, maps, and drawings as appropriate) of
the scale, timing and mitigation of all construction related
aspects of the development.

b)   
Site hours of operation.

c)   
Numbers, frequency, routing and type of vehicles
visiting the site (including measures to limit delivery journeys on
the SRN during highway peak hours such as the use vehicle booking
systems etc).

d)   
Measures to ensure that HGV loads are adequately
secured.

e)   
Travel plan and guided access/egress and parking
arrangements for site workers, visitors and deliveries.

f)    
Sheeting of loose loads and wheel washing and other
facilities to prevent dust, dirt, detritus etc. from entering the
public highway (and means to remove if it occurs).

g)   
The anticipated number, frequency and types of
vehicles used during construction.

h)   
The method of access and egress and routing of
vehicles during construction.

i)     
The parking of vehicles by site operatives and
visitors.

j)     
The loading and unloading of plant, materials and
waste.

k)   
The storage of plant and materials used in
construction of the development.

l)     
The erection and maintenance of security
hoarding.

m)  
The provision and utilisation of wheel washing
facilities and other works required to mitigate the impact of
construction upon the public highway (including the provision of
temporary Traffic Regulation Orders).

n)   
The site lighting scheme and control of light spill
to adjoining residential properties.

o)   
Measures to control noise, vibration and dust,
including from piling operations.

p)   
Detailed measures to manage flood risk and water
pollution, both on and off the site, during the construction
phase.

q)   
Details of public engagement both prior to and
during construction works.
Reason:
This pre-commencement condition is
required to ensure that the A259 continues to be an
effective part of the national system of routes for through traffic
in accordance with section 10 of the Highways Act 1980, and to
safeguard the living conditions of nearby residents, protect the
natural environment and satisfy the reasonable requirements of road
safety, in accordance with Policies OSS4 (ii), CO6 (ii), EN5 &
TR3 of the Rother Local Plan Core Strategy and Policy DEN4 of the
Rother Development and Site Allocations
Local Plan.  

 

5.       
No development hereby permitted shall
take place (including demolition, ground works and site clearance)
until a scheme to address the management and/or safe disposal of
any asbestos and asbestos containing materials in the existing
building(s) at the site has been submitted to and approved in
writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall be
informed by a full asbestos survey undertaken by a competent person
and shall be implemented as approved.
Reason: This pre-commencement condition is required
in the interests of protecting human health, in accordance with
Policy OSS3 (viii) of the Rother Local Plan Core Strategy and
Policy DEN7 of the Rother Development and Site Allocations Local
Plan.

 

6.       
No development hereby permitted shall take place
(excluding demolition and site
clearance) until a scheme for the provision of foul water
drainage works has been submitted to and approved in writing by the
Local Planning Authority, and the foul water drainage works to
serve the development shall be carried out and retained in
accordance with the approved details. Occupation of the food store
should align with the delivery of any sewerage network
reinforcement required to ensure that adequate wastewater network
capacity is available to adequately drain the development.

Reason: To
secure the satisfactory foul water drainage of the site,
including to avoid flood risk and to prevent water pollution,
in accordance with Policies OSS3 (ii), SRM2
(i & ii) & EN7 of the Rother
Local Plan Core Strategy and Policies F1 & H6 (e) of the Rye
Neighbourhood Plan. 

 

7.       
No development hereby permitted shall take place
(excluding demolition and site
clearance) until details of a surface water drainage system
have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local
Planning Authority. The surface water drainage system shall
incorporate the following: 

a)   
Surface water discharge rates not exceeding
greenfield runoff rates for all rainfall events, including those
with 1 in 100 (+20% for climate change) annual probability of
occurrence. Evidence of this (in the form of hydraulic
calculations) shall be submitted with the detailed drainage
drawings and construction details. The hydraulic calculations shall
take into account the connectivity of
the different surface water drainage features.

b)   
The details of pollution prevention
measures.

c)   
The details of the outfall of the proposed
attenuation storage and how it connects into the watercourse and
sewer shall be provided as part of the detailed design. This shall
include cross sections and invert levels.

d)   
The condition of the of the sewer and ordinary
watercourse which will take surface water runoff from the
development shall be investigated before discharge of surface water
runoff from the development is made. Any required improvements to
the condition of the watercourse shall be carried out prior to
construction of the outfall.

e)   
The detailed design shall include information on how
surface water flows exceeding the capacity of the surface water
drainage features will be managed safely.

f)    
The detailed design of the attenuation storage shall
be informed by findings of groundwater monitoring between autumn
and spring. The design shall leave at least 1m unsaturated zone
between the base of the ponds and the highest recorded groundwater
level. Alternatively, or if this cannot be achieved, details of
measures which will be taken to manage the impacts of high
groundwater on the drainage system shall be provided based upon
robust assumption of high ground water levels.

g)   
A maintenance and management plan for the entire
drainage system, which ensures the designed system takes into account design standards of those
responsible for maintenance. The maintenance and management plan
shall cover the following:

-      
Clearly state who will be responsible for managing
all aspects of the surface water drainage system, including piped
drains.

-      
Evidence of how these responsibility arrangements
will remain in place throughout the lifetime of the
development.
The
development shall not be occupied until evidence (including
surveys, as built plans, site records and photographs as necessary)
demonstrating that the surface water drainage system has been
constructed in accordance with the approved details, has been
submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority. The approved maintenance and management plan for the
entire surface water drainage system shall remain in place for the
lifetime of the development.
Reason: To
ensure that surface water runoff from the development is managed
safely, avoiding flood risk and preventing water pollution, in
accordance with Policies SRM2 (ii & iii) & EN7 of the
Rother Local Plan Core Strategy, Policy DEN5 of the Rother
Development and Site Allocations Local Plan and Policy F1 of the
Rye Neighbourhood Plan. 

 

8.       
No development hereby permitted shall take place
(including demolition, ground works and site clearance) until a
Precautionary Working Method Statement for reptiles, great crested
newts and other amphibians, terrestrial mammals and invasive
non-native plant species and for protection of local habitats and
associated species, including The Brede Valley Local Wildlife Site
(LWS), watercourses and coastal and floodplain grazing marsh, has
been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority. The content of the method statement shall include the
following:

a)   
purpose and objectives for the proposed works;

b)   
detailed design(s) and/or working method(s)
necessary to achieve stated objectives (including, where relevant,
type and source of materials to be used);

c)   
extent and location of proposed works shown on
appropriate scale maps and plans;

d)   
timetable for implementation, demonstrating that
works are aligned with the proposed phasing of construction;

e)   
persons responsible for implementing the
works;

f)    
initial aftercare and long-term maintenance (where
relevant); and

g)   
disposal of any wastes arising from the
works.
The works
shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and
shall be retained in that manner thereafter.
Reason:
This pre-commencement condition is required in the interests of
protecting ecology and biodiversity, in accordance with Policy EN5
(ix) of the Rother Local Plan Core Strategy and Policy DEN4 (ii) of
the Rother Development and Site Allocations Local Plan.

 

9.       
No development hereby permitted shall take place
(including demolition, ground works and site clearance) until Air
Quality and Emissions Mitigation Assessments – prepared by a
suitably qualified person and in accordance with the Air Quality
and Emissions Mitigation Guidance for Sussex (2021) – have
been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority. If air quality and emissions mitigation
measures are required, then these shall be implemented prior to the
commencement and/or first occupation of the development in
accordance with an air quality and emissions mitigation measures
scheme which has been submitted to and approved in writing by the
Local Planning Authority.
Reason:
This pre-commencement condition is required to minimise the effect
of the development on air quality and to protect human health, in
accordance with Policy OSS3 (viii) of the Rother Local Plan Core
Strategy and Policy DEN7 of the Rother Development and Site
Allocations Local Plan.  
 
OTHER
CONDITIONS:
 

10.     
Demolition or construction works, and
construction related deliveries, shall take place only between the
hours of:

·        
8am to 6pm on weekdays;

·        
8am to 1pm on Saturdays; and

·        
not at any time on Sundays, or on Bank or
Public Holidays.
Reason: To
safeguard the living conditions of nearby residents, in accordance
with Policy OSS4 (ii) of the Rother Local Plan Core
Strategy.

 

11.     
If, during development, contamination not previously
identified is found to be present at the site then no further
development shall be carried out until a remediation scheme and
timetable detailing how this contamination will be dealt with has
been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning
Authority. The remediation scheme shall include: 

a)   
An appraisal of remediation options.

b)   
Identification of the preferred
option(s).

c)   
The proposed remediation objectives and remediation
criteria.

d)   
A description and programme of the works to be
undertaken including the verification plan.
The
remediation scheme shall be sufficiently detailed and thorough to
ensure that upon completion the site will not qualify as
contaminated land under Part IIA of the Environmental Protection
Act 1990 (as amended) in relation to its intended use. The
remediation works shall be carried out in accordance with the
approved scheme and upon completion a verification report prepared
by a suitably qualified contaminated land practitioner shall be
submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority before the development is occupied.
Reason: In
the interests of protecting human health and the natural
environment, in accordance with Policy OSS3 (viii) of the Rother
Local Plan Core Strategy and Policy DEN7 of the Rother Development
and Site Allocations Local Plan.

 

12.     
The development hereby permitted shall be carried
out in accordance with the Stage 2 Flood Risk Assessment (Job No:
10620), produced by GTA Civils & Transport Ltd, Second Issue
dated 30 May 2024, and the Flood Risk Assessment Addendum (Job No:
10620), produced by GTA Civils & Transport Ltd, dated 24
September 2024. In particular, the development shall be carried out
in accordance with the following mitigation measures detailed
within these documents:

·        
Ground finished floor levels shall be set no lower
than 3.45 metres above Ordnance Datum (AOD).

·        
The proposed scheme for floodplain volume
compensation outlined in Sections 15 -17 and Appendix C of the
Flood Risk Assessment Addendum.
These
mitigation measures shall be fully implemented prior to occupation
of the development and subsequently in accordance with the
scheme’s timing/phasing arrangements. The measures detailed
above shall be retained and maintained thereafter throughout the
lifetime of the development.
Reason: To
reduce the risk of flooding to the development and future occupants
and to prevent flooding elsewhere by ensuring that compensatory
storage of flood water is provided, in accordance with Policies EN6
& EN7 of the Rother Local Plan Core Strategy and Policies F1
& H6 (d) of the Rye Neighbourhood Plan.

 

13.     
All ecological measures and/or works shall be
carried out in accordance with the mitigation measures detailed at
section 5.2 of the Preliminary Ecological Appraisal (File
reference: 22_1710_Report_MF_IR) – dated 13/10/2025, prepared
by GreenLink Ecology Ltd, and detailed
at section 6.1 of the Ecological Impact Assessment (File reference:
22_1710_ReportX02_MF_IR) – dated 13/10/2025, prepared by
GreenLink Ecology Ltd.
Reason: In
the interests of protecting ecology and biodiversity, in accordance
with Policy EN5 (ix) of the Rother Local Plan Core Strategy and
Policy DEN4 (ii) of the Rother Development and Site Allocations
Local Plan.

 

14.     
The development hereby permitted shall be carried
out in accordance with the tree protection measures detailed on
Drawing Number 2096-KC-XX-YTREE-TPP01RevD (TREE PROTECTION PLAN),
dated 13.06.25.
Reason: To
protect the character and appearance of the area, in accordance
with Policy OSS4 (iii) of the Rother Local Plan Core
Strategy.

 

15.     
No development above slab level shall take place
until an Ecological Design Strategy (EDS) addressing measures to
protect local habitat (including coastal and floodplain grazing
marsh) during the operational phase, and ecological compensation
and enhancement, to include the provision of soft landscaping of
value to wildlife, and the provision of bat and bird bricks/boxes,
has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority. Enhancement measures shall be informed by the
recommendations in section 5.3 of the Preliminary Ecological
Appraisal (File reference: 22_1710_Report_MF_IR) – dated
13/10/2025, prepared by GreenLink
Ecology Ltd. The EDS shall include the following:

a)   
purpose and conservation objectives for the proposed
works;

b)   
review of site potential and constraints;

c)   
detailed design(s) and/or working method(s) to
achieve stated objectives;

d)   
extent and location/area of proposed works on
appropriate scale maps and plans;

e)   
type and source of materials to be used where
appropriate, e.g. native species of local provenance;

f)    
timetable for implementation demonstrating that
works are aligned with the proposed phasing of development;

g)   
persons responsible for implementing the
works;

h)   
details of initial aftercare and long-term
maintenance;

i)     
details for monitoring and remedial measures;
and

j)     
details for disposal of any wastes arising from
works.
The EDS
shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and all features shall be retained in that
manner thereafter.
Reason: In
the interests of conserving and enhancing biodiversity, in
accordance with Policy EN5 (ix) of the Rother Local Plan Core
Strategy and Policy DEN4 (ii) of the Rother Development and Site
Allocations Local Plan. 

 

16.     
No development above slab level shall take place until full details of a
continuous acoustic barrier – which shall have a minimum
height of 3.5m and a minimum surface density of 10 kg/m²
– to be constructed along the north-east side of the food
store delivery/loading bay yard, have been submitted to and
approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details
shall include the following:

a)   
Scaled elevations and sections of the acoustic
barrier detailing construction materials and showing the
relationship with adjacent ground levels and the loading
bay.

b)   
The acoustic barrier shall be designed to have an
acoustic durability of 0.25 dB/year maximum loss and a non-acoustic
durability of at least 20 years to ensure that adequate mitigation
is maintained over the longer term.

c)   
A maintenance and management plan for the acoustic
barrier, which shall cover the following:

-      
Clearly state who will be responsible for
maintaining the acoustic barrier.

-      
Evidence of how these responsibility arrangements
will remain in place throughout the lifetime of the
development.
The
development shall not be occupied until the acoustic barrier has
been constructed in accordance with the approved details. The
acoustic barrier as approved and the approved maintenance and
management plan for the acoustic barrier shall remain in place for
the lifetime of the development.  
Reason: To
safeguard the living conditions of nearby residents, in accordance
with Policy OSS4 (ii) of the Rother Local Plan Core
Strategy.

 

17.     
No development above slab level shall take place
until the following details have been submitted to and approved in
writing by the Local Planning Authority and the development shall
thereafter be carried out and maintained in accordance with the
approved details:

a)   
Specifications and samples of the materials to be
used in the external surfaces of the food store
building.

b)   
Drawings to a scale of 1:20 fully detailing the
proposed windows and doors (including their interface with the
adjoining wall), roof verges and eaves.
Reason: In
the interests of securing a visually attractive development that
makes a positive contribution to the character and appearance of
the area, in accordance with Policies OSS4 (iii), EN1, EN2 (ii)
& EN3 of the Rother Local Plan Core Strategy, Policies DEN1
& DEN2 of the Rother Development and Site Allocations Local
Plan and Policies H6 (b) & D1 of the Rye Neighbourhood
Plan. 

 

18.     
No development above slab level shall take place
until full details of the hard and soft landscaping scheme,
including a timetable for implementation, have been submitted to
and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These
details shall include:

a)   
Hard landscaping:

-      
Boundary treatments (including details of a solid
boarded fence to be erected around the car park perimeter where it
is adjacent to existing residential properties).

-      
Specifications and samples of all materials proposed
for hard-surfacing.

-      
Details of all minor structures proposed in the
public-realm including street-furniture, refuse or other storage
units and signage.

b)   
Soft landscaping:

-      
Detailed planting plans, supported by written
material as necessary, setting out the mix of species, their size,
number and planting densities as appropriate (the plants should be
native species and of local provenance).

-      
The detail of all new trees, including their
species, sizes, quantity, positions, the time of planting and how
they will be protected and maintained until successfully
established in accordance with BS5837:2012 “Trees in Relation
to Design, Demolition and Construction –
Recommendations” (the trees should be native species and of
local provenance).

-      
Details of the measures to be employed to ensure the
successful establishment of all planting, including new trees, and
its maintenance into the future for a period of five years from the
date of the planting being undertaken shall also be provided.
Regard shall be had to the measures suggested in BS 8545:2014
“Trees: From Nursery to Independence in the Landscape –
Recommendations”.
All hard
and soft landscaping works shall be undertaken in accordance with
the approved landscaping works. Any trees or plants that, within a
period of five years after planting, are removed, die or are
seriously damaged shall be replaced by others of the same species,
size and number as originally proposed.
Reason: In
the interests of securing a visually attractive development that
makes a positive contribution to the character and appearance of
the area, and to safeguard the living conditions of nearby
residents, in accordance with Policies OSS4 (ii & iii), EN1,
EN2 (ii) & EN3 of the Rother Local Plan Core Strategy, Policies
DEN1 & DEN2 of the Rother Development and Site Allocations
Local Plan and Policies H6 (b) & D1 of the Rye Neighbourhood
Plan. 

 

19.     
No lighting shall be installed until a Lighting
Design/Mitigation Strategy to limit the impact of light pollution
from artificial light on the amenities of neighbouring residential
properties, the High Weald National Landscape and biodiversity, has
been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority. The strategy shall relate to both internal and external
lighting at the site and be prepared by a competent person having
regard to the Institute of Lighting Professionals guidance notes on
The Reduction of Obtrusive Light and Bats and Artificial Lighting
At Night. It shall provide details as
appropriate and shall include the following matters:

a)   
Identify those areas/features on site that are
particularly sensitive for bats and that are likely to cause
disturbance in or around their roosting sites or along important
routes used to access key areas of their territory, for example,
for foraging.

b)   
Identify the neighbouring residential properties
that are likely to be impacted by artificial light from the
site.

c)   
Provide appropriate lighting contour plans and
technical specifications etc. so that it can be clearly
demonstrated that the internal and external lighting will not
disturb or prevent the bats using their territory or having access
to their roosting sites or adversely impact the living conditions
of the residents of the neighbouring residential
properties.
The
Lighting Design/Mitigation Strategy shall be implemented as
approved prior to first occupation and maintained thereafter for
the lifetime of the development.
Reason: In
the interests of mitigating the effects of lighting on
biodiversity, on the landscape and on the living conditions of
nearby residents, in accordance with Polices OSS4 (ii & iii),
EN1 & EN5 (ix) of the Rother Local Plan Core Strategy and
Policies DEN1, DEN2, DEN4 (ii) & DEN7 (ii) of the Rother
Development and Site Allocations Local Plan.     

 

20.     
A Landscape and Ecological Management Plan (LEMP)
shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority prior to the occupation of the development hereby
permitted. The content of the LEMP shall include the
following:

a)   
description and evaluation of features to be
managed;

b)   
ecological trends and constraints on site that might
influence management;

c)   
aims and objectives of management;

d)   
appropriate management options for achieving aims
and objectives;

e)   
prescriptions for management actions, together with
a plan of management compartments;

f)    
preparation of a work schedule (including an annual
work plan capable of being rolled forward over a five-year
period);

g)   
details of the body or organisation responsible for
implementation of the plan; and

h)   
ongoing monitoring and remedial measures.
The LEMP
shall also include details of the legal and funding mechanism(s) by
which the long-term implementation of the plan will be secured by
the developer with the management body(ies) responsible for its delivery. The plan shall
also set out (where the results from monitoring show that
conservation aims and objectives of the LEMP are not being met) how
contingencies and/or remedial action will be identified, agreed and
implemented so that the development still delivers the fully
functioning biodiversity objectives of the originally approved
scheme. The approved plan shall be implemented in accordance with
the approved details.
Reason: In
the interests of securing the long-term management of retained,
enhanced or newly created habitats arising from the development, in
accordance with Policy EN5 (v & ix) of the Rother Local Plan
Core Strategy and Policy DEN4 (ii & iii) of the Rother
Development and Site Allocations Local Plan.

 

21.     
The development hereby permitted shall not be
brought into use until the archaeological site investigation and
post-investigation assessment (including provision for analysis,
publication and dissemination of results and archive deposition)
– which shall be undertaken in accordance with the programme
set out in the approved written scheme of investigation – has
been completed and approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority.
Reason: To
ensure that the archaeological and historical interest of the site
is safeguarded and recorded, in accordance with Policy EN2 (vi) of
the Rother Local Plan Core Strategy.

 

22.     
The development hereby permitted shall not be
occupied until the mown grass footpath link shown to the south-west
of the development on the approved drawings has been provided in
accordance with a detailed specification of works (including
ongoing maintenance and management arrangements) for this area,
which has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local
Planning Authority. The footpath shall thereafter be retained and
maintained for that use and shall not be used for any other
purpose.
Reason: To
provide an attractive and well-designed footpath link, and to
minimise the impacts of the development on biodiversity, in
accordance with Policies EN5 & TR3 of the Rother Local Plan
Core Strategy, Policy DEN4 of the Rother Development and Site
Allocations Local Plan and Policy T1 of the Rye Neighbourhood
Plan.

 

23.     
The development hereby permitted shall not be
occupied until motor vehicle parking areas have been provided in
accordance with the approved drawings, and the areas shall
thereafter be retained for that use and shall not be used other
than for the parking of motor vehicles.
Reason: To
ensure that the development functions well and does not prejudice
highway safety, in accordance with Policies CO6 (ii) & TR4
(iii) of the Rother Local Plan Core Strategy.

 

24.     
The motor vehicle parking spaces shall measure at
least 2.5m by 5m (add an extra 50cm where spaces abut walls/fences)
and for disabled spaces 3.6m by 5m (add an extra 50cm where spaces
abut walls/fences).
Reason: To
ensure that the development functions well and does not prejudice
highway safety, in accordance with Policy CO6 (ii) of the Rother
Local Plan Core Strategy.

 

25.     
The development hereby permitted shall not be
occupied until secure covered cycle parking areas have been
provided in accordance with the approved drawings, and the areas
shall thereafter be retained for that use and shall not be used
other than for the parking of cycles.
Reason: To
promote the use of cycling and sustainable travel choices, in
accordance with Policies TR2 & TR3 of the Rother Local Plan
Core Strategy and Policy T1 of the Rye Neighbourhood
Plan.

 

26.     
No part of the development hereby permitted shall be
occupied until a Travel Plan has been submitted to and approved in
writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Travel Plan, once
approved, shall thereafter be implemented by a Travel Plan
co-ordinator as specified within the approved document. The Travel
Plan shall be completed in accordance with the latest guidance and
good practice documentation as published by the Department for
Transport and/or as advised by the Highway Authority and shall
include a “measures-based” approach that:

a)   
Sets specific targets/outcomes.

b)   
Outlines the measures to achieve those
targets.

c)   
Details any remedies or sanctions if targets are not
met.
Reason: To
promote sustainable travel choices, in accordance with Policies TR2
& TR3 of the Rother Local Plan Core Strategy and Policy T1 of
the Rye Neighbourhood Plan.
 

27.     
No part of the development hereby permitted shall be
occupied until a real-time bus passenger information TFT display
screen to display real-time bus departure information for The
Tillingham Bridge and The Deals bus
stops has been installed within the food store in accordance with
details which have been submitted to and approved in writing by the
Local Planning Authority, and the approved display screen shall
thereafter be retained.
Reason: To
promote sustainable travel choices, in accordance with Policies TR2
& TR3 of the Rother Local Plan Core Strategy and Policy T1 of
the Rye Neighbourhood Plan.

 

28.     
No part of the development hereby permitted shall be
occupied until a Servicing Management
Plan (SMP) – setting out the arrangements for the loading and
unloading of deliveries, in terms of location and frequency, and
setting out the arrangements for the collection of refuse
– has been submitted to and approved in writing by the
Local Planning Authority. Thereafter the approved SMP shall be
implemented and adhered to in full for the lifetime of the
development unless the Local Planning Authority gives written
consent to any variation.
Reason: To
ensure that the development functions well and does not prejudice
highway safety, in accordance with Policy CO6 (ii) of the Rother
Local Plan Core Strategy.

 

29.     
Prior to first occupation of the
development hereby permitted, the Flood Warning & Evacuation
Plan Retail Store (Ref: 10620), produced by
GTA Civils & Transport Ltd, First Issue dated 4 February 2025,
shall be put in place and it shall thereafter be retained
throughout the lifetime of the development unless the Local
Planning Authority gives written consent to any
variation.
Reason: To
reduce the risk to life in a flood event, in accordance with
Policies EN6 & EN7 of the Rother Local Plan Core Strategy and
Policies F1 & H6 (d) of the Rye Neighbourhood Plan.

 

30.     
The food store hereby permitted shall not be
occupied until solar PV panels have been provided in accordance
with details which have been submitted to and approved in writing
by the Local Planning Authority. The solar PV panels shall
thereafter be retained. 
Reason: To
mitigate and adapt to climate change, in accordance with Policy
SRM1 of the Rother Local Plan Core Strategy. 

 

31.     
The food store hereby permitted shall not be open to
customers outside the following hours:

·        
8am to 10pm Monday to Saturday.

·        
9am to 5pm on Sundays.
Reason: To
safeguard the living conditions of nearby residents, in accordance
with Policy OSS4 (ii) of the Rother Local Plan Core
Strategy.

 

32.     
Deliveries shall be received or dispatched from the
food store only between the hours
of:

·        
7am to 10.30pm from Monday to Saturday;
and

·        
8am to 8pm on Sundays.
In
addition:

·        
There shall be no movement of goods pallets or roll
cages on open areas of the delivery/loading bay yard.

·        
There shall be no audible reversing beepers to be
used outside the food store opening hours.

·        
Refrigeration units on vehicles should be switched
off when vehicles enter the delivery/loading bay yard.
Reason: To
safeguard the living conditions of nearby residents, in accordance
with Policy OSS4 (ii) of the Rother Local Plan Core
Strategy.

 

33.     
No mezzanine floor shall be inserted within the food
store building hereby permitted.
Reason: To
control the size of the food store, thereby ensuring the
development functions well and does not prejudice highway safety,
in accordance with Policy CO6 (ii) of the Rother Local Plan Core
Strategy.

 

34.     
The rating level of sound emitted from any fixed
plant/machinery associated with the development hereby permitted
shall not exceed 44 dB LAeq,15min at any noise sensitive property
between the hours of 0700-1900hrs, and shall not exceed 35 dB
LAeq,15min at any noise sensitive property between the hours of
1900-0700hrs. All measurements shall be made in accordance with the
methodology of BS 4142:2014+A1:2019 (Methods for rating and
assessing industrial and commercial sound) and/or its subsequent
amendments. Where access to the nearest noise sensitive property is
not possible, measurements shall be undertaken at a location agreed
in writing by the Local Planning Authority and corrected to
establish the noise levels at the nearest noise sensitive property.
Any deviations from the assessment time interval stipulated above
shall be agreed in writing by the Local Planning
Authority.
Reason: To
safeguard the living conditions of nearby residents, in accordance
with Policy OSS4 (ii) of the Rother Local Plan Core
Strategy.

 

35.     
The premises shall be used for Class E(a) purposes
only and for no other purpose (including any other purpose in Class
E of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes)
Order 1987 (as amended), or in any provision equivalent to that
Class in any statutory instrument revoking and re-enacting that
Order with or without modification).
Reason: To
ensure the vitality and viability of Rye town centre, in accordance
with Policy EC7 (i) of the Rother Local
Plan Core Strategy.   
 
NOTES:
 

1.       
This planning permission is the subject of a planning obligation
under Section 106 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as
amended).

 

2.       
The development granted by this planning permission is subject to
the Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL). Full details will be set
out in the CIL Liability Notice which will be issued in conjunction
with this decision. All interested parties are referred to 
https://www.rother.gov.uk/planning-and-building-control/planning-policy/community-infrastructure-levy-cil-2/
for further information and the charging schedule.

 

3.       
The effect of paragraph 13 of Schedule 7A of the
Town and Country Planning Act 1990 is that planning permission
granted for the development is deemed to have been granted subject
to the condition (“the biodiversity condition”) that
development may not begin unless:

a.   
A Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to the
planning authority; and

b.   
The planning authority has approved the
plan.
The Local
Planning Authority, for the purposes of determining whether to
approve a Biodiversity Gain Plan if one is required in respect of
this permission would be Rother District Council. As such, the
development granted by this planning permission is subject to the
Biodiversity Gain Condition, which requires a Biodiversity Gain
Plan to be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local
Planning Authority before development commences. A Biodiversity
Gain Plan template is available on the Government website

https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/biodiversity-gain-plan,
and this should be completed and submitted to the Local Planning
Authority to demonstrate how the development will achieve 10%
Biodiversity Net Gain.  Advice on how
BNG may be delivered is also available on the Government
website: 
https://www.gov.uk/guidance/understanding-biodiversity-net-gain.

 

4.       
The Applicant/Developer is reminded that, under the
Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017 (as amended)
and the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 (as amended), it is an
offence to (amongst other things): deliberately capture, disturb,
injure, or kill great crested newts; damage or destroy a breeding
or resting place; intentionally or recklessly obstruct access to a
resting or sheltering place. Planning permission for a development
does not provide a defence against prosecution under this
legislation. Should great crested newts be found at any stage of
the development works, then all works should cease, and a
professional and/or suitably qualified and experienced ecologist
(or Natural England) should be contacted for advice on any special
precautions before continuing, including the need for a
licence.

 

5.       
The Applicant/Developer is reminded that all species
of bats are fully protected under the Wildlife and Countryside Act
1981, as amended, and The Conservation of Habitats and Species
Regulations 2017, as amended, making them European Protected
Species. Under the Regulations, it is an offence to: deliberately kill, injure, disturb or capture
bats; damage or destroy their breeding sites and resting places
(even when bats are not present); or possess, control of transport
them (alive or dead). Under the Act, it is an offence to
intentionally or recklessly: disturb bats while they occupy a
structure or place used for shelter or protection; or obstruct
access to a place of shelter or protection. Planning consent for a
development does not provide a defence against prosecution under
these Regulations or this Act.

 

6.       
The Applicant/Developer is reminded that, under the
Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981, as amended (section 1), it is an
offence to remove, damage or destroy the nest of any wild bird
while that nest is in use of being built. Planning consent for a
development does not provide a defence against prosecution under
this Act.

 

7.       
This development involves work to the public highway
(strategic road network) that can only be undertaken within the
scope of a legal Agreement between the Applicant and National
Highways (as the strategic highway company appointed by the
Secretary of State for Transport). Planning permission in itself does not permit these works. It is the
Applicant’s responsibility to ensure that before commencement
of any works to the public highway, any necessary Agreements under
the Highways Act 1980 are also obtained (and at no cost to National
Highways). Works to the public highway will normally require an
agreement, under Section 278 of the Highways Act, with National
Highways. Any new access to the SRN (completely new or materially
altered) also requires specific consent from National Highways
under S175B of the Highways Act 1980. Advice on this matter can be
obtained from the Spatial Planning Team, National Highways, Bridge
House, Walnut Tree Close, Guildford, Surrey, GU1 4LZ. Email
PlanningSE@nationalhighways.co.ukTel
0300 123 5000.

 

8.       
Land Drainage Consent (LDA 1991) will be
required from the Romney Marshes Area
Internal Drainage Board for the outfall
to the Ordinary Watercourse.

 

9.       
The Applicant/Developer’s attention
is drawn to the advice provided by the Environment Agency and
Southern Water in their consultation responses to the planning
application, which are available to view on the Council’s
website 
https://www.rother.gov.uk/planning-and-building-control/.

 

10.     
The Applicant/Developer is reminded of the trading hours rules for
large shops in England and Wales. For shops over 280sqm:

·        
Can open on Sundays but only for 6
consecutive hours between 10am and 6pm.

·        
Must close on Easter Sunday.

·        
Must close on Christmas Day.

 
NATIONAL PLANNING POLICY FRAMEWORK:  In accordance
with Paragraph 39 of the National Planning Policy Framework, the
Local Planning Authority has worked in a positive and pro-active
way with the Applicant by identifying matters of concern within the
application (as originally submitted) and negotiating acceptable
amendments to address those concerns. This has enabled the Local
Planning Authority to grant planning permission for a sustainable
development.
 
(Councillor Creaser declared an Other Registerable Interest in
this matter in so far as she was the Council’s
appointed Board Member on the Romney Marshes
Area Internal Drainage Board who had commented on the site and she
lived near the site but was indifferent and in accordance with the
Members’ Code of Conduct remained in the meeting during the
consideration thereof.)
 
(Councillor Mier declared an Other Registerable Interest in this
matter in so far as he was the Council’s appointed
Board Member on the Romney Marshes Area Internal
Drainage Board who had commented on the site and in accordance with
the Members’ Code of Conduct remained in the meeting during
the consideration thereof.)
topline: The Planning Committee has granted planning permission for a food store in Rye, despite concerns about its impact on the town centre.

This
application was presented to the Planning Committee as the
Applicant was a close relation of a member of staff at Rother
District Council. 
 
The
Planning Committee was supportive of the officer’s
recommendation, subject to the conditions as outlined
below. 
 
Councillor Gray moved the motion to GRANT (Full Planning
Permission) subject to conditions and this was seconded by
Councillor Chowdhury. 
 
The
motion was declared CARRIED (8 for / unanimous).
 
DECISION: GRANT (FULL PLANNING
PERMISSION)
 
SUBJECT TO
CONDITIONS:
 

1.         
The development hereby permitted shall be begun
before the expiration of three years from the date of this
permission.?
Reason: In
accordance with section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act
1990 (as amended by section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory
Purchase Act 2004).?

 

2.         
The development hereby permitted shall be carried
out in accordance with the following approved plans and
details:
Drawing No.
25.710/01 – Existing Floor Plan, Elevations and Site Location
Plan – dated October 2025
Drawing No.
25.710/02A – Proposed Floor Plan, Elevations and Site Block
Plan – dated October 2025
Reason: For
the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper
planning.

 

3.         
The external materials to be used in the
construction of the extension hereby permitted shall be as
detailed within the application submissions, unless otherwise
agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To
ensure that the development is in character with its surroundings
in accordance with Policy OSS4(iii) of the Rother Local Plan Core
Strategy and Policy DHG9(ii) of the Rother Development and Site
Allocations Local Plan.

 

4.         
No windows or other openings shall be installed
within the side (east) elevation of the extension (including
garage) hereby approved.
Reason: ﻿To
protect the residential amenities of the neighbouring
property in accordance with Policy OSS4 (ii) of the Rother
Local Plan Core Strategy and Policy HG9(i) of the Rother Development and Site Allocations
Local Plan.
 
NATIONAL PLANNING
POLICY FRAMEWORK: In accordance with
Paragraph 39 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), the
Council has worked in a positive and pro-active way and has imposed
planning conditions to enable the grant of planning
permission.

content:
This
application was presented to the Planning Committee as it was
located on Council owned land.
 
The
Planning Officer clarified that the proposal description described
should read: “Construction of a workshop area for car and van
repairs and general maintenance (Use Class B2), rather than
“caravan” as stated in the report.
 
The
Planning Committee was supportive of the officer’s
recommendation, subject to conditions as outlined below.
 
Councillor Stanger moved the motion to GRANT (Full Planning
Permission) subject to conditions and this was seconded by
Councillor Gray. 
 
The
motion was declared CARRIED (8 for / unanimous)
 
DECISION: GRANT (FULL PLANNING
PERMISSION)
 
SUBJECT TO
CONDITIONS:
 

1.         
The development hereby permitted shall be begun
before the expiration of three years from the date of this
permission.
Reason: In
accordance with section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act
1990 (as amended by section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory
Purchase Act 2004).

 

2.         
The development hereby permitted shall be carried
out in accordance with the following approved plans:
Existing/Proposed Floor Plans, Elevations & Site Plans
- 25.704/01, dated August 25
Reason: For
the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper
planning.

 

3.         
The materials to be used in the construction of the
external surfaces of the development hereby permitted shall be in
accordance with that described in the application unless an
alternative finish is first submitted to and approved in writing by
the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To
maintain the characteristics of the existing buildings and the
local area, in accordance with Policies OSS4 (iii) and EN3 of the
Rother Local Plan Core Strategy and DEN1 of the Development and
Site Allocations Plan.

 

4.         
No plant, with the
exception of the vehicle lift, whether externally
located or which vents externally, including but not limited to
extraction units or air source heat plant, shall be provided,
installed or operated within/on the building hereby approved
without a further planning permission from the Local Planning
Authority.
Reason: To preserve the residential amenities of the
locality including Barn Field Terrace and London Road to the east,
in accordance with Policy OSS4 (ii) of the Rother Local Plan Core
Strategy.
 

NATIONAL PLANNING POLICY
FRAMEWORK: In accordance with
Paragraph 39 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), the
Council has worked in a positive and pro-active way and has granted
planning permission subject to conditions.

content:
This
application was presented to the Planning Committee as it was a
Council application.
 
It
was commented that completing the works could be deemed wasteful,
as the building might be sold as part of the 2028 Local Government
Reorganisation and Devolution.  The
Chair stated that this was not a material planning consideration
and should not be taken into account.
 
The
Planning Committee agreed that the proposal would provide an
accessible, ramped entrance from the car park to the Amherst
building and lift.  The Planning
Committee therefore supported the officer’s recommendation,
subject to the conditions outlined below.
 
Councillor Drayson moved the motion to GRANT (Full Planning
Permission) subject to conditions and this was seconded by
Councillor Stanger. 
 
The motion was declared CARRIED
(6 for / 2 abstained)
 
DECISION: GRANT (FULL PLANNING
PERMISSION)
 
SUBJECT TO CONDITIONS:
 

1.       
The development hereby permitted shall be begun
before the expiration of three years from the date of this
permission.
Reason: In
accordance with section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act
1990 (as amended by section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory
Purchase Act 2004).

 

2.       
The development hereby permitted shall be carried
out in accordance with the following approved plans and

3.       
The materials to be used in the construction of the

Reason: To ensure the

NATIONAL PLANNING

content:
Consideration was given to the report of the Chief Executive on
Rother District Council’s refreshed Council Plan 2025-29 (CP)
at Appendix A to the report.  The
refreshed CP was built on the adopted December 2024 version,
developed through resident, stakeholder and staff engagement, and
had been revised for greater clarity, focus and strategic
alignment.  The CP had been scrutinised
by the Overview and Scrutiny Committee (OSC) on 26 January 2026 and
a copy of the Minute arising from the OSC meeting had been appended
to the report for Cabinet’s consideration (Appendix G). The
OSC had made several rewording suggestions in three areas of the
Action Plan (AP).
 
The
CP set the short, medium and long-term vision (up to 2040) for the
district and provided a steer for future
plans and strategies and aligned with relevant Council
documents.  The vision to 2040,
strategic outcomes to 2029 and focused on four key objectives,
namely A Thriving Local Economy; Live Well Locally; Green to the
Core; and Fit for the Future.
 
All
key changes were outlined within the report and focused on
clarifying how the priorities were presented, shifting toward a
more outcome focused approach.  The
Thriving Local Economy section had been strengthened following
targeted work on regeneration and tourism.  Other content had been streamlined to keep the CP
strategic, with operational detail moved to supporting delivery and
action plans.
 
The
AP at Appendix B to the report showed progress in 2024/25 and
outlined the next steps for 2026.  Of
the 64 actions, 50 were on track and 14 were due to start in 2026.
Cabinet was supportive of the OSC’s rewording suggestions and
for the Town of Culture applications by Bexhill and Battle and 1066
Country Marketing events in relation to the Bayeaux Tapestry and
the Year of the Normans to be included.
 
The
Annual Progress report at Appendix C highlighted the
Council’s key achievements over the past year, including the
new Welcome Centre at Camber Sands, distribution of £1.7m in
Disabled Facilities Grants, and national recognition for its
climate work.  These successes reflected
the commitment of Members, staff, and partners.  The report would be shared with partners,
including Rother’s parish and town councils and residents via
MyAlerts and the press.
 
Progress against the Council Plan was measured through
indicators drawn from sources such as the Council’s Key
Performance Indicators and the State of the District
report.  Of the 35 measures for 2024/25,
18 were rated green, six amber, four red, and seven had no rating
due to baseline data still being established.  Many measures were district-wide which fell
outside the Council’s direct control.
 
Some
Cabinet Members raised concerns about the closure of three GP
surgeries in the district (two in Bexhill and one in Robertsbridge)
and delays with the provision of three new GP surgeries on
Council-owned land. Officers would update Members after the
meeting.
 
After discussion, Cabinet was supportive of the refreshed CP, AP
and Annual Progress report for 2025, with the OSC’s suggested
rewording and recommended that they be formally approved and
adopted.  They considered and agreed
that the Equalities Objectives as detailed at Appendix E to the
report, be approved for consultation.
 
Cabinet congratulated officers on their hard work in preparing
and producing the CP.
 
RECOMMENDED: That the refreshed
Council Plan 2025-2029, its Action Plan, with suggested amendments,
and the Annual Progress report for 2025 be approved and
adopted.
 
AND
 
*RESOLVED: That the Equality
Objectives be approved for consultation.
 
*The
RESOLVED part of this Minute is subject to the call-in
procedure under Rule 16 of the Overview and Scrutiny Procedure
Rules by no later than 4:00pm on 12 February 2026.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve and adopt Rother District Council's refreshed Council Plan 2025-2029, its Action Plan, and the Annual Progress report for 2025.

purpose:
To consider and agree the Council's Medium
Term Financial Plan
content:
Consideration was given to the report of the Director of
Resources on the draft Budget for 2026/27 and Medium Term Financial Plan 2026-2029
(MTFP).  The Budget had been scrutinised
by the Overview and Scrutiny Committee (OSC) on 26 January 2026 and
a copy of the Minute arising from the OSC meeting had been appended
to the report for Cabinet’s consideration (Appendix
H).  The OSC had recommended that the
winter car park tariffs in Camber remained the same as the previous
year and that the annual contribution to the Rye Harbour Nature
Reserve be reinstated in the Budget.
 
Appended to the report were details of the proposed savings
(Appendix A), Growth Proposals (Appendix B), Summary Budget 2026/27
(Appendix C), Capital Programme (CP) (Appendix D), Fees and Charges
(Appendix E), MTFP (Appendix F) and Consultation Report (Appendix
G).
The
following key issues were highlighted:
 

·     
it had been anticipated that £1.181m would be
drawn from reserves during 2025/26, despite good progress against
the agreed savings target;

·     
£694,000 was being supported by the General
Reserve (GR); including the additional in-year overspend forecast,
would reduce the GR to £3.819m. The anticipated loss incurred
on the Hermes Property Fund of £420,000 and potential further
£900,000 related to aborted capital schemes could reduce this
further to £2.5m;

·     
the CP continued to be under review and was
constantly being updated and reforecast; a comprehensive update on
several projects was included within the report, along with the
Community Infrastructure Levy allocations.  It was noted that £7.6m of National Lottery
Heritage Funding had been awarded to support the installation of
energy efficiency products to the De La Warr Pavilion
(DLWP).  The total approved CP budget
for this project was now £26.1m;

·     
the CP totalled £191m, with £124m spend
in this and future years.  The projected
outturn as at 31 March 2026 for 2025/26
was anticipated to be c£48m, with the remaining balance being
spread over future years;

·     
overspends in 2025/26 were anticipated to reoccur in
2026/27;

·     
an 3.8% inflation rate was assumed for 2026/27 which
would only be applied to expenditure budgets where the Council had
a contractual commitment to an uplift;

·     
a 3% staff pay increase had been budgeted;

·     
no anticipated savings from the devolution project
had been incorporated within the Budget at this time;

·     
the Government’s 2025 Fair Funding Review
(FFR) reset the Business Rates Retention System.  As a result, all East Sussex Councils had
withdrawn from the 2026/27 Business Rates Pooling, as it no longer
offered any benefit;

·     
the local government financial settlement aligned
with FFR principles and the autumn policy statement.  It introduced updated formulas and data, which
focused on deprivation to assess council needs and set funding
levels.  It also provided a multi-year
settlement with major grant changes;

·     
no announcements were made regarding support for
Local Government Reorganisation and Devolution;

·     
for 2026/27, to ensure the Council remained within
the referendum limit, it was assumed that a Council Tax increase of
2.99% to £216.95 (increase £6.30) would be agreed for a
Band D property;

·     
no change was proposed to the Council Tax Reduction
Scheme;

·     
most fees and charges had been increased by 3.8%,
with a few exceptions where charges had increased between 5% to
10%; and

·     
the uplift in funding for 2026/27, as well as a
reduction in pension contribution rates, had aided the overall
budget position for the year, resulting in the Council being
in a position to set the Budget, without
drawing from reserves. (Appendix C to the report incorporated the
latest budget position following the settlement.)
 
The
budget consultation closed on 5 January 2026, and the results were
set out in Appendix G to the report. A late response had been
submitted by Camber Parish Council and circulated to Members before
the meeting. The consultation had received a total of 83 responses,
with the majority of questions receiving
around 40 responses; Members were concerned that this was not a
true reflection of the views of all residents.
 
Some
Members of Cabinet raised concerns about the proposed DLWP grant
reduction. After some discussion, Cabinet agreed to recommend
notice be given to the DLWP of a 10% grant reduction from 2027/28,
but that the decision was taken subject to a further report to
Cabinet on the DLWP funding and future options
appraisal.
 
Cabinet paid tribute to officers for managing to present a
balanced budget without drawing from reserves and were supportive
of the OSC’s recommendations.
 
RECOMMENDED: That the amendment to the
Capital Programme, as detailed in Appendix D and paragraphs 50 to
58 of the report, be adopted.
 
AND
 
*RESOLVED: That:
 

1)    
the draft Budget for and Medium-Term Financial Plan,
as noted in the report and appendices, be the basis for preparing
the final 2026/27 budget and Council Tax recommendations to full
Council;
 

2)    
the Council Tax for 2026/27 at Band D be increased
by £6.30 (2.99%) and set at £216.95;
 

3)    
the fees and charges outlined in Appendix E to the
report, be approved;
 

4)    
the Director of Resources be authorised to sign the
National Lottery Heritage Fund grant offer in respect of the De La
Warr Pavilion award of £7.6m outlined in paragraph 54 of the
report;
 

5)    
winter car park tariffs in Camber remain the same as
the previous year;
 

6)    
the annual contribution to the Rye Harbour Nature
Reserve be 
reinstated in the Budget; and
 

7)    
notice be given to the De La Warr Pavilion (DLWP) of
a 10% grant reduction from 2027/28, subject to a further report to
Cabinet on the DLWP funding and future option appraisal.
 
*The
RESOLVED parts of this Minute are subject to the call-in
procedure under Rule 16 of the Overview and Scrutiny Procedure
Rules by no later than 4:00pm on 12 February 2026.
